title: clearModuleFeatures is dead in prod and its named scope deletes the legacy bucket
body:
## Summary
`clearModuleFeatures` has zero production callers, and its named-project scope also deletes every unattributed (`project_id = ''`) row of the module, which every other project reads.

## Description
src/lib/feature-matrix-db.ts:561 deletes with `projectScopeSql` (own OR ''), while its sibling `pruneReviewSnapshots` (src/lib/feature-matrix-db.ts:778) is deliberately exact-scope because a project 'must not be able to evict another project's - or the shared legacy bucket's - history'. The docstring says a clear 'can never reach another project's matrix', yet legacy rows are visible to every project. The only consumers are 6 test files (16 references) using it as fixture cleanup. Fixed = remove the export and give the tests an exact-scope DELETE helper (or, if a caller is wanted later, scope it to exact project_id).

## Flow
- grep clearModuleFeatures outside src/__tests__ -> only its definition
- a named-project call DELETEs that project's rows plus all '' rows of the module
- every other project's matrix loses those legacy rows

## Expected impact
No user-visible change today (no prod caller); removes a latent cross-project delete. Could break: the 6 tests that use it, migrated in the same change.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - remove a dead export whose scope contradicts its sibling
Before: production callers 0; test refs 16 in 6 files; clear=own+legacy vs prune=exact
After: export removed; tests use an exact-scope helper; one scope rule
Method: simulation - zero-consumer grep run; not built: spans 6 test files outside this round's paths (M)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/feature-matrix-db.ts:561-567 (DELETE ... AND (project_id = ? OR project_id = ''))
src/lib/feature-matrix-db.ts:778-791 (prune: project_id = ? exact)
grep -rln clearModuleFeatures src e2e scripts -> feature-matrix-db.ts + 6 files under src/__tests__ only
instrument: grep (non-test hits must be 0) + the 6 feature-matrix test files green after migration

title: Choose and assert the SQLite synchronous level (durability contract)
body:
## Summary
The bootstrap never sets or asserts `PRAGMA synchronous`, so the durability half of the WAL contract is whatever the engine default is.

## Description
src/lib/db.ts:66-79 now asserts the journal mode (commit 2436d8cf), but the sync level - the clause that decides whether a power cut can lose the last commits - is never chosen, written down or checked. registry embedded-db / journal-and-durability-modes: 'choose explicitly, write the choice down with its reasons, assert it at boot'. NORMAL under WAL is the common desktop choice but loosens durability vs FULL; FULL costs a per-commit fsync. That is a product decision, not a sweep's.

## Flow
- boot -> journal_mode=WAL -> no synchronous pragma -> engine default
- operator decides FULL vs NORMAL; code sets it, reads it back, warns on mismatch, documents it

## Expected impact
Visible only in crash recovery; NORMAL may lose the last moments of work on power cut, FULL may slow write-heavy paths.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a stated, asserted durability level
Before: synchronous: unset, unasserted, undocumented
After: set + read back + logged + documented in docs/architecture/state-and-persistence
Method: simulation - the recorded deviation (registry-map, evaluatedAt 2026-10-25) names it; no instrument decides a product trade-off
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
src/lib/db.ts:65-79 (bootstrap: journal_mode + foreign_keys only)
.ai/registry-map.json database-layer/embedded-db: state deviation, evidence src/lib/db.ts:66
instrument: operator decision FULL vs NORMAL; then a boot test asserting PRAGMA synchronous reads back the chosen level

title: Seven append-only tables have no retention owner
body:
## Summary
session_log, session_analytics (stores the full prompt text), telemetry_snapshots, cli_spend, audio_gen_usage, module_scans and eval_findings are written on every run and deleted by nothing.

## Description
grep `DELETE FROM <table>` outside tests: 0 hits for each of the 7 (request_log and build_history do have one). review_snapshots already got a per-module cap (MAX_SNAPSHOTS_PER_MODULE, src/lib/feature-matrix-db.ts:630) - the precedent. registry embedded-db golden path: 'Storage grows forever unless something owns pruning'. Several readers aggregate all-time (cli_spend dashboard totals, audio totals), so a retention rule changes what those surfaces report: a product decision and a deletion of user data.

## Flow
- every CLI run -> session_analytics + session_log + cli_spend rows
- nothing deletes them -> pof.db grows monotonically
- operator picks per-table rules (cap, age, rollup-then-prune)

## Expected impact
Bounded DB size and faster all-history scans; could break all-time totals unless a rollup preserves them.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - bounded storage
Before: tables with a delete path: 0 of 7
After: 7 of 7 with a stated rule (or an explicit keep-forever note)
Method: simulation - grep counted; row counts of the real DB not read (containment rule)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: irreversible
evidence:
grep -rn "DELETE FROM <t>" src --include=*.ts (non-test): session_log 0, session_analytics 0, telemetry_snapshots 0, cli_spend 0, audio_gen_usage 0, module_scans 0, eval_findings 0; request_log 1, build_history 1
src/lib/db.ts:436-454 (session_analytics.prompt TEXT NOT NULL)
instrument: operator retention rule per table; then a storage-accounting test (row count after N inserts stays <= cap)

title: feature_matrix DDL is hand-copied three times in db.ts
body:
## Summary
The feature_matrix column set is declared three times (bootstrap CREATE, the project-key rebuild, the 'improved' rebuild), each by hand.

## Description
src/lib/db.ts:96, src/lib/db.ts:626 and src/lib/db.ts:753 repeat the same 15 column definitions; only the UNIQUE clause legitimately differs. A column added to the bootstrap and forgotten in a rebuild DDL is dropped by that rebuild on an older DB. Commit 26507d19 now gates the copy LISTS against the live schema, but not the rebuild DDLs. Fixed = one `featureMatrixDdl(table, uniqueClause)` builder used by all three.

## Flow
- count column-definition blocks for feature_matrix in db.ts -> 3
- extract one builder; the three call it with their UNIQUE clause
- gate: the rebuilt table's PRAGMA table_info equals the bootstrap's

## Expected impact
Prevents a future silent column loss during a rebuild migration; touches migration code, so it needs the key-migration and improved-rebuild tests green.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source of truth for the table shape
Before: hand-copied DDL bodies: 3
After: 1 builder, 3 call sites; table_info parity test
Method: simulation - copies counted; not built this round (migration code, wants an isolated run of the migration suites)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: table_info parity test: after migrateFeatureMatrixImprovedStatus and migrateFeatureMatrixProjectKey on a pre-'improved' fixture DB, columns equal the fresh bootstrap's

title: Hot static queries re-prepare per call while prepareCached exists
body:
## Summary
55 static-SQL `.prepare()` sites across five context *-db files recompile on every call, though db.ts ships `prepareCached` for exactly this.

## Description
src/lib/db.ts:870-892 notes better-sqlite3 has no statement cache and memoizes per connection; 11 call sites repo-wide use it. src/lib/catalog-db.ts (9), src/lib/pipeline-db.ts (3), src/lib/cli-spend-db.ts (11), src/lib/feature-matrix-db.ts (23) and src/lib/audio-asset-db.ts (15, takes db explicitly) prepare static SQL per call; e.g. getEntity/getLifecycle run per entity in catalog derivations. Gain is per-call compile time, unmeasured here.

## Flow
- time N calls of getEntity / listTracks with per-call prepare vs prepareCached on a containment DB
- adopt prepareCached at the sites that measure better

## Expected impact
Lower latency on catalog/feature-matrix hot paths; low break risk (same SQL).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer statement compiles on hot paths
Before: static per-call prepare sites: 55; per-call cost: unmeasured
After: cached at hot sites; timing delta recorded
Method: simulation - sites counted; no timing taken
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
grep -c ".prepare(" (non-interpolated): catalog-db 9, pipeline-db 3, cli-spend-db 11, feature-matrix-db 23, audio-asset-db 15
src/lib/db.ts:870-892 prepareCached
instrument: microbench: 10k getEntity/listTracks calls per-call prepare vs prepareCached on a containment DB

title: POST /api/feature-matrix accepts non-string filePaths elements
body:
## Summary
The full-upsert route checks only `Array.isArray(f.filePaths)`, while the import route validates `z.array(z.string())`.

## Description
src/app/api/feature-matrix/route.ts:70 lets `[1, null, {}]` through to upsertFeatures, which stores it. Commit d0bb782c made the reader drop non-strings, so nothing crashes now, but the bad elements are still persisted and silently discarded on read. The import route (src/app/api/feature-matrix/import/route.ts:58) already rejects them. Fixed = the route rejects a non-string element with 400 (or reuses the import schema).

## Flow
- POST {features:[{...,filePaths:[1]}]} -> 200, row stored with [1]
- fix: 400 naming the bad row

## Expected impact
Callers sending malformed rows get a 400 instead of silent data loss; could break a caller relying on lenient acceptance (none known).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - write-side validation agrees with the import route
Before: element validation on the 2 write routes: 1 of 2
After: 2 of 2
Method: simulation - read the two validators; route is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: route test: POST with filePaths [1] expects 400 (red before, green after)

title: audio-db-conn ensures its schema once per process, not per connection
body:
## Summary
`getAudioDb()` gates its DDL on a module boolean, while every other lazy-schema module keys the guard on the live Database handle.

## Description
src/lib/audio-db-conn.ts:16 `let ready = false`; src/lib/catalog-db.ts:12, src/lib/pipeline-db.ts:9 and src/lib/cli-spend-db.ts:27 key on the handle 'so a swapped connection re-runs the DDL'. With the boolean, a test (or any future reconnect) that swaps the connection gets an audio DB without audio tables. Fixed = key on the handle like the siblings.

## Flow
- swap the getDb connection after one getAudioDb() call
- getAudioDb() returns the new handle without creating audio_sets

## Expected impact
Test-only today (getDb never swaps in prod); prevents 'no such table' on a reconnect.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one schema-guard rule across *-db modules
Before: guards keyed on handle: 3 of 4
After: 4 of 4
Method: simulation - read the four guards; file is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: test: mock getDb to return handle A then B; after both getAudioDb() calls, B has audio_sets (red before)
